newsitem.title: UK: Iceland says expects lower profits in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Iceland says expects lower profits in 1996.

text.p: Iceland Plc said on Tuesday it expected to report lower profits for 1996 and said overall like for like sales in the second half to date were down by 0.5 percent.

"Profitability will be affected by further investment of our buying margin in Pricewatch during the second half, and by the loss of sales arising from temporary store closures for refurbishment," the company said in a statement.

The group said that overall like for like sales in the second half to date were down by 0.5 percent. But it noted the second quarter saw a decline of 1.0 percent. There had been some improvement in like for like performance of frozen food.
Iceland earlier reported first half pre-tax profits of 29.8 million stg, down from 33.6 million and below most analysts' forecasts ranging from 30.0 million to 30.5 million stg.
The group said long term investment was continuing, including a 10 million stg two-year information technology programme. Over 250 stores are scheduled for refurbishment, mainly in the second half.
Iceland expects to open 30 new stores this year, 10 fewer than originally forceast. Capital expenditure should therefore be lower than previously estimated at about 68 million stg.
